names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 9 Οκτωβρίου, «Όσιος Πέτρος «ο από στρατιωτών»», with the rank word left off; the epithet «ο από στρατιωτών» is the page's own. It glosses the name from πέτρα, the rock.
The bare name out of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 1773, headed «Петр Галатийский, Константинопольский, прп.», with the rank word and the two epithets left off.

floruit.note: saint.gr: «έζησε στα χρόνια του βασιλιά Θεοφίλου του εικονομάχου (829 μ.Χ.)», and «ο βασιλιάς Βασίλειος ο Μακεδών, το έτος 867 μ.Χ., τον έπεισε να κατοικήσει στο μοναστήρι του Αγίου Φωκά»

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, 9 октября ст. ст. — «Прп. Петра Галатийского (IX).»
source.note: No rank is read onto him. His line closes the day's second paragraph, which carries no icon; the day's two icons are both in the first, and belong to the apostle James and to Andronicus and his wife.

attestations.note: The Russian names him for his province where the Greek names him for the soldiers: «Прп. Петра Галатийского», and its index page heads him «Петр Галатийский, Константинопольский, прп.», adding Constantinople. The Greek life gives both — a man of the province of the Galatians who was made a count and became a monk — so the two entries are one man and the epithets are two readings of the same life. Its «(IX)» agrees with the `floruit` the Greek page's years gave this folder, 829 to 867. The Russian carries no life for him. He is **not** the `peter-of-galatia` this corpus already holds, whom all four churches keep on 1 February: that one lived in the fourth and fifth centuries, shut himself in a tomb at Antioch and died in 429. Two men, four centuries apart, whom one English epithet would merge — which is why the English name of this folder stays the Greek one and the life says «Peter the Galatian» where it translates the Russian line.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).
